input_candidate_proposals.reason: The petitioners' claimed original letting to the respondent supplies the asserted baseline tenant identity against which any later transfer of possession to the firms would be assessed.
The petitioners directly allege subletting to two firms carrying on business independently, which is candidate evidence for parting with possession but is not itself an established fact.
The respondent's two-distinct-tenancies account tends to defeat the proposition that one tenancy was later parted with to third parties.

The respondent's own pleading places each firm in tenancy and possession of a separate shop, providing candidate evidence of possession by persons or firms other than the asserted original tenant, while leaving the legal character disputed.
The respondent's claimed participation as partner in both firms is candidate evidence that he retained participation or control, which tends against complete divestment of possession.

The respondent's account of a pre-2008 single tenancy later divided into two tenancies is candidate evidence of a change in possessory or tenancy arrangement, although the respondent characterizes that change as lawful new tenancies.
The respondent dates the alleged separation and creation of two tenancies to March 2008, which is after the statutory cutoff.
The respondent likewise places the asserted division into two tenancies in 2008, supporting the temporal condition if that is the legally relevant arrangement.
The petitioners expressly allege that no written permission was obtained for the alleged subletting.
The respondent alleges landlord consent and a written understanding dated 10.03.2008, directly contesting the absence-of-written-consent condition, subject to authenticity, timing, and legal effect.

target_refs.quote: first ingredient of Sec. 14(1)(b) of D.R.C. Act is satisfied as the physical as well as legal possession of the tenanted premises has been parted with

target_witnesses.reason: The target court expressly adopted the first section 14(1)(b) ingredient and found parting with both physical and legal possession.

target_refs.quote: Sh. Ramji Lal Goel and Sh. Bhajan Lal Goel got retired from the firm w.e.f. 01.04.1992
the physical as well as legal possession of the tenanted premises has been parted with

target_witnesses.reason: The target court accepted a 1992 retirement fact in the reasoning immediately preceding its express finding of parting with possession; 1992 is after the statutory cutoff of 9 June 1952.

target_refs.quote: no cogent and convincing evidence documentary or oral has been produced before this court which prove that such consent in writing was given
ingredient in respect of not taking of consent of landlord in writing is also satisfied

target_witnesses.reason: The target court expressly found the no-written-consent ingredient satisfied because the respondent did not produce cogent and convincing proof of written consent; this is labeled burden not carried rather than a finding that the asserted writing never existed.
